A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AF-Retriever research. Their complete text, algorithms, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original AF-Retriever benchmark results, component ablations, reranker experiments, and runtime measurements in Section 4 and Appendix A.6.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and adds broader reranker evaluations, manual semantic-error assessments, and expanded latency results.

M1.justification: The eight-step pipeline, incremental scope expansion, hybrid retrieval, three reranking strategies, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained. Additional prompt instructions document target conditioning and output restrictions already described in the method; they do not establish a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the PRIME, MAG, and AMAZON SKBs and their synthetic and human-generated QA coverage. The added diagnostic and latency studies reuse these domains and tasks.

E2.justification: v4 removes PASemiQA, mFAR, and MoR from the averaged comparison in Table 2, while retaining their dataset-specific comparisons in Table 4. Splitting the earlier Table 3 into zero/one-shot and supervised tables introduces no new external comparators.

E3.justification: Supplementary protocols expand substantially: reranker evaluation covers eight backbones rather than two, and a manual audit examines 50 generated queries per dataset. Timing switches from local A100/vLLM inference to a Cerebras API setup and adds parallel pointwise evaluation. Appendix A.6 also replaces the general medium-effort default with medium for parsing and low for reranking; this reported revision does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix A.7 add manual assessment of whether generated Cypher queries express the intended question, pipeline error-flow analyses, and categorized examples. Broader reranker comparisons and an accuracy–latency analysis substantially extend diagnostics. Earlier component ablations and alpha-sensitivity curves are largely retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point metrics and descriptive latency summaries. The new manual audit reports category proportions, without adding repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and component-ablation scores remain unchanged, but substantial reranker, semantic-error, and latency results are added. GPT OSS 20B's PRIME pairwise hit@1 is reported as 47.8 in v2 Table 18 and 42.0 in v4 Table 6, which explicitly describes end-to-end evaluation; its hit@5/MRR breakdowns disappear. Runtime results are replaced under different inference conditions, so they do not establish same-setting speedups.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, grounding algorithm, transitivity assumption, and reranking complexity comparison in Table 1 are retained. No new formal results, proofs, or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The modular SKB-retrieval contribution, zero/one-shot performance claims, and claimed 32.1% average first-hit advantage remain unchanged. The abstract and conclusion retain their substantive claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations distinguishing syntactic validity from semantic adequacy, identifying when graph filtering cannot constrain questions, and explaining complementary VSS retrieval. It expands model-dependent accuracy and latency interpretations and broadens the stated robust alpha range from 0.5–0.8 to 0.4–0.85.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds explicit predicted-target and single-query/output instructions to the documented Cypher prompt. Runtime hardware and inference-service documentation changes, and reasoning effort is specified by stage. The public code-access statement remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained, including distinctions from 4StepFocus and dataset-specific fine-tuning approaches such as GraphRAFT. Abbreviation and wording edits do not change those relationships.

P1.justification: Editing concentrates on the introductory framing and evaluation narrative, including new Sections 4.1–4.2, corrected cross-references, and a clearer running question. Most method, related-work, and conclusion prose remains unchanged; the new error-analysis prose also contains repetition.

P2.justification: v4 adds three error-flow diagrams, an accuracy–latency figure, an expanded reranker table, and three example tables. It separates benchmark tables and moves existing analyses into the main text. The retained sensitivity curves receive revised axes and annotations, constituting substantial visual restructuring.

improvement.justification: The broader reranker tests, semantic-error audit with examples, and accuracy–latency comparisons make component choices and failure modes better supported than in v2. These improve diagnostic and practical completeness while the core method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged. Loss of GPT OSS 20B hit@5/MRR detail and uneven editing temper the benefit.
